questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I study English I wanted to go to an English speaking country. I also wanted to go to a place where there was a lot to experience culturally and where I could easily travel to other parts of the country. I narrowed it down by looking though the course catalogue of the different universities and chose based on what I was most interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and everything was told to us via email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly email and introduction seminars when we arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me since I lived with people I already knew. But I would always recommend applying for university housing as it is much easier if you don't know anyone in Bristol.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was great for me because I paid much less rent than I would have done had I lived in student accommodation but it also meant that it was slightly harder to make friends in the beginning because you didn't live with people from university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for all the courses you would like (I think max 6) and then they give you three of those. It's pretty straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email and they were quick to answer

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got courses I wanted!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Only apply for courses you're really interested in so that you don't end up with something you don't want. And take your time looking through their course catalogue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Only BA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar to that of UCPH but there were fewer contact hours so I had to do more self study than in Copenhagen. But the approaches to teaching were the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Shakespeare 
Shakespearean Tragedy
Pitching Productions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It really depends on what you're interested in but the two Shakespeare courses I had were brilliant. I got so much out of them and they really helped me understand Shakespeare on a whole. There are many courses in literature if that's what you're interested in and all the tutors are so inspiring and eager to teach and help you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None other than having to replace my student ID when I lost it (15 pounds)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books are less expensive than in Denmark, otherwise everything is mostly the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can literary find a society for every single interest. Whatever you're interested in, there will be something for you. Sometimes there are even multiple societies for the same interest (four drama societies for example).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can't think of one specifically but just go on the Student Union website and see what catches your eye. There's literally something for every interest. I can highly recommend it as it's a great way to make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London is only a 1.5 hour train ride away and I would definitely recommend seeing a West End show at least once. Bath is also only a 12 minute train ride away and is a lovely little city that everyone should visit. They even have a Jane Austen museum! Cardiff isn't far either and Oxford and Cambridge are also great fun and not too far away for a day trip. In Bristol you should absolutely see a show at the Hippodrome and at the Bristol Old Vic. They also have a youth drama club at the Bristol Old Vic which I can highly recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy since it's not too different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many societies as you can and go to the events organised by the university. It can be difficult to make friends in class because there isn't much time to talk so try and find things to do with other people outside of your lessons.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was really difficult but I had also lived in Bristol before.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation for the Arts and diversity, particularly in Bristol, was really great to see.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Put yourself out there and don't be shy to ask people if they want to grab coffee or hang out. Everyone is really sweet but because you're often entering an established group they might not think to ask you. Choose classes that you find interesting and that you can't take at UCPH. Get involved with things that are happening at the university, there are always lots of events where you can meet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go to everything in your intro week to get to know people and make friends across courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything I learned in my Shakespeare classes. They have really been rewarding and made me understand his work much better.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think making friends was definitely the hardest challenge. Although it wasn't impossible and I also made friends it took a lot of effort.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
